Oh See Threee

Audio-Source-Oscillator 5-Voice Analog Pitch Synth

Oh See Threee gives you the hands-on controls of an analog synth, with your performance as the sound source. The audio you feed it takes the place of the usual sine, triangle, or square-wave oscillator. The idea is to let you play an octave effect like an instrument while keeping the character of what you put into it.

Emulations of vintage analog octave-down and octave-up circuits create two voices below your input and two above it, with a shapeable unison voice in the middle. Blend them into a deep synth growl or a bright, glitchy choir. Give each voice its own level, pan, and delay to pan them across time and the stereo field, then use the filters to shape the tone.

The front panel is laid out like a synth. Use the Pitch wheel to sweep through the five voices with Cycle on, and the Mod wheel to bring in movement from the LFO, envelope follower, and noise source.

Quick start

  1. Insert Oh See Threee on a stereo audio track or bus. Play audio through its stereo input to drive the octave voices.
  2. Pick a factory preset in the amber display, or try Wub Wub for a sub-focused starting state. Its two upper faders are stored at −60 dB.
  3. In Voices, bring up Sub 2, Sub 1, Uni, Up 1, or Up 2. Use Dry to blend in the direct input. The Uni voice has its own pan, delay, filter, and modulation.
  4. Set the Volume knob while watching the output meter. If tracking chatters or misses notes, open Inside and adjust Hysteresis, Gate, Detector Gain, and Sub Range for the source.
  5. Shape the upper voices with Pre LPF Up1, Pre LPF Up2, and Up Edge. Add delay, pan, and modulation after the basic balance feels right.

Drag knobs, faders, and wheels to adjust them. Value bubbles show the setting as you move a control. Click Inside to open the lid and Replace Cover to return to the front. Drag the bottom-right grip to resize the editor proportionally.

Front panel

Modulation

The three glass windows show the live LFO, ENV, and Noise sources. Each column has four depth faders. Positive and negative depths move the destination in opposite directions. Set a depth to 0% to turn off that connection.

Printed control Range or choices Use
Wave Sine, Triangle, Saw Up, Saw Down, Square, Random Choose the LFO shape.
Sync Free / Sync Free uses Rate in Hz. Sync offers six host-tempo divisions from 1/16 through 2 bars. If host tempo is unavailable, the processor uses 120 BPM. Random always runs freely in Hz.
Rate 0.05–20 Hz free, or six synced divisions Set LFO speed. In Sync mode, turn clockwise for faster divisions. Choose 2 bars, 1 bar, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, or 1/16.
Phase 0–360° Offset a periodic LFO. Random has no fixed phase, so Phase is disabled for that shape.
Atk, Rel Attack 1–250 ms, release 5–1,000 ms Set the envelope follower's attack and release.
Sens 0–6× Scale how strongly input level drives the envelope modulation source.
Texture 0–100% Smooth the Noise source at low values. Raise Texture for faster, more jittery movement.
Dly, Pan, Whl, Flt Each −100% to +100% For each source, set depth to delay time, stereo pan, Pitch Wheel position, and filter cutoff. Delay modulation can create pitch movement.
Mod wheel 0–100% Scale every Env, LFO, and Noise depth together. At 0%, those modulation depths have no effect.

The Whl depth faders become active when you turn on Cycle. Watch the traces to see the shape of each modulation source.

Voices

Each voice column has a Pan knob and level fader. The five voices from Sub 2 through Up 2 each have a Delay knob.

Voice controls Range or display Use
Level fader −60 to +12 dB Set each voice's mix level. The meter beside the fader shows activity in that voice.
Pan C, L 1–100, R 1–100 Place a voice in the stereo field. C is center. L and R indicate the side and distance.
Delay 0–250 ms Offset Sub 2, Sub 1, Uni, Up 1, or Up 2 in time by the chosen number of milliseconds.

Dry takes the input directly to its own level, pan, and optional low-pass filter. Uni follows the voice processing path at the input pitch.

Filters and output

Each low-pass filter row has a cutoff knob, a Res control, and an On rocker. The rocker lights when the filter is active. Raise Res to emphasize frequencies around the cutoff.

Row Cutoff range Res range Applies to
Sub Freq 80–4,000 Hz Q 0.50–8.00 Sub 1 and Sub 2
Uni Freq 80–12,000 Hz Q 0.50–8.00 Uni
Up Freq 200–8,000 Hz Q 0.50–8.00 Up 1 and Up 2
Dry Freq 80–12,000 Hz Q 0.50–8.00 Dry blend

Volume sets the final output from −60 to +12 dB. The analog VU dial follows the stereo output level, and its Peak lamp marks recent high peaks. Use the On / Bypass rocker to pass the input through at its original level. Some hosts also provide a separate plug-in bypass control.

Pitch controls

Control Range or choices Use
Cycle Off / On Enables the on-screen Pitch wheel to move through Sub 2 → Sub 1 → Uni → Up 1 → Up 2.
Pitch wheel 0–100% Choose a position in the voice range while Cycle is on. The wheel springs back to its midpoint when you release it.
X-Fade Off / On With Cycle on, blend smoothly between adjacent voices. With it off, the wheel switches between voices.

Inside

Open the lid to tune the detector, divider, voice trims, and upper-octave generation. These controls are saved with the sound and can also be automated by the host.

Tracking and divider switches

Printed control Range or switch positions Use
Hysteresis 0–100% Sets how far the input must swing before the detector counts another cycle. A low setting can make loud, bright notes trip extra cycles. A high setting can make soft notes miss cycles.
Gate −60 to 0 dB Mutes the octave voices below the input threshold. Raise it to reduce chatter between notes. Listen for clipped note tails as you raise it.
Detector Gain 1–10× Boosts the signal feeding the detector. Raise it if weak or complex input is difficult to track.
Sub Range 50–600 Hz Sets the low-pass cutoff on the signal feeding the sub-octave generators. Lower settings reduce brightness.
SW1 / Sub Mode Polarity Switch (Off), Magnitude Reapply (On) Choose how Sub 1 is formed. Polarity Switch flips the wave each cycle. Magnitude Reapply rectifies and reapplies it.
SW2 / Sub2 Mode Cascade (/4) (Off), Re-detect (On) Cascade divides again from the same detector. Re-detect tracks Sub 1's output for Sub 2.
SW3 / Order Filter → Delay (Off), Delay → Filter (On) Set the order of each voice's tone filter and delay. The difference is most apparent when a filter cutoff is being modulated.

The DIP levers point up for On. The brief guides beside each control describe common tracking tradeoffs.

Voice trims and feeds

Use the five small Trims pots to balance voice gain ahead of the front-panel faders. Then set the mix with the faders.

Pot Range Use
Unison, Sub 1, Sub 2 −18 to +18 dB Fine gain trim for the named voice.
Up 1, Up 2 −25.4 to +10.6 dB Fine gain trim for the named upper voice. A 0 dB setting includes the internal compensation for rectifier level loss.
Sub2 Feed −24 to +24 dB Set how strongly Sub 1 feeds the Sub 2 divider.
Up2 Feed −24 to +24 dB Set how strongly Up 1 feeds the second rectifier.

Upper-octave voicing

The upper voices use nonlinear rectification. Use the pre-filters to tune how much of the input's upper harmonics reach each rectifier.

Printed control Range or switch Use
Pre LPF Up1 200–8,000 Hz Low-pass before the +1 rectifier. Lower settings limit the source harmonics entering that stage.
Pre LPF Up2 200–16,000 Hz Independent low-pass before the +2 rectifier.
Up Edge 0–100% Set the knee of both upper rectifiers. Turn up for a harder, fuzzier edge or down for a rounder result.
Up2 High-pass 20–8,000 Hz, with a separate On switch Turn on the high-pass filter to reduce Up 1 bleed-through in the Up 2 voice. Adjust the cutoff to bring Up 2 forward.
Up2 Auto Level On / Off Bring Up 2 closer to the input's loudness and apply a fast peak guard to that voice.

To type a setting, click the printed value beside an Inside pot, enter a number, then press Return. Drag the pot for continuous adjustment. Select Replace Cover to close the board.

Presets and sessions

Use the amber preset display to load a preset. The < and > buttons move to the previous and next entry. The display shows Unsaved until the sound has a preset name. User and factory presets live under Documents/Sunbunny/Oh See Threee/Presets as .preset files.

A/B comparison and Init

Button What it does
A, B Recall one of two sound slots. The first time the editor opens for a new plug-in instance, both slots start from the current sound. Switching slots stores the current sound in the slot you leave and recalls the other.
A→B Copy A's sound and preset name to B. If B is selected, the copied sound becomes active immediately.
Save Type a name in the preset display, then select Save. Using an existing name replaces that preset file.
Init Reset the active slot's sound parameters to the plug-in defaults and return the display to Unsaved.
Info Open the product information panel.

A/B slots live in the plug-in instance, including while the editor window is closed. When you reopen a DAW session, it recalls the active sound and the panel Bypass state. To keep both sounds between sessions, select each slot and save it under its own preset name. The panel Bypass rocker applies across both slots and is saved with the DAW session.

Three factory starting points

These starting points describe the presets' stored settings. Choose one for the octave balance you want, then adjust it for your source.

Preset Useful first look
Wub Wub Sub 1 is at −1.2 dB and Sub 2 at −2.9 dB, with both upper voices at −60 dB. Its Saw Up LFO is synced to 1/8 and modulates Delay and Filter.
Double Analog Up Both sub voices are at −60 dB. Up 1 is at −7.2 dB and Up 2 at −11.3 dB. The Up2 pre-filter is set to 5,564 Hz.
Spliced Tracks Cycle and X-Fade are on. The five voice levels range from −0.6 to +4.6 dB. Its LFO is synced to 1/2 and modulates Delay, Wheel, and Filter.

Installation and support

Formats and installation

The current release workflow targets Windows x64 VST3 and Linux x86_64 VST3. This guide covers the redesigned full edition. Check the files supplied with your release and use a host that supports stereo VST3 audio effects. The source also defines a Standalone target.

For manual installation, close the DAW and copy the entire Sunbunny Oh See Threee.vst3 bundle to the VST3 folder for your system. Reopen the DAW and rescan plug-ins.

  • Windows C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3\
  • Linux ~/.vst3/ (create the folder if needed)

If a Windows installer accompanies your download, follow its prompts and use its Oh See Threee entry in Windows Installed apps to remove it. For a manual ZIP install, close the DAW and remove only the plug-in bundle from the folder where you copied it. User presets are stored separately under Documents/Sunbunny/Oh See Threee/Presets and remain unless you remove them yourself.

Windows builds may require the latest supported Microsoft Visual C++ v14 Redistributable (x64). If the host reports a missing MSVCP140.dll or VCRUNTIME140.dll, install Microsoft's supported x64 runtime from its current redistributable information or x64 installer.

Limits and help

Oh See Threee uses up to 250 ms of per-voice delay. It reports a zero tail duration to the host, so extend a render past the last note by at least the longest active delay and listen to the ending.

For a product question, visit GitHub Discussions. For a bug, open GitHub Issues and include the plug-in version, operating system, host and version, sample rate, buffer size, the controls involved, and steps to reproduce the problem. Remove private audio or project material before attaching anything. See the third-party notices and the included Sigmar One font license.

About

Hello! I’m Phillip Adkins, the musician and developer behind Sunbunny. I’ve been writing code and developing audio and machine learning algorithms for 15+ years.

I’m heavily jazz influenced, love classical impressionism, and have an unhealthily large collection of weird effects pedals I’m constantly tweaking. You’ll hear that mix in my guitar-centric instrumental music and in the plug-ins I make, including Oh See Threee.
